Every production-reading test keeps an explicit generous timeout (60_000), not Bun's 5000 ms default.

The spec's remedy Constraint item (4) ships as a regression guard in the test file, keyed on the arguments rather than on a source string, so it survives this bundle's close and runs in CI forever: a test that scans scripts/validate-record-retirement.test.ts's own source and fails when any call site that can spawn the validator — through the runValidator helper or a direct spawnSync naming the SCRIPT constant — carries a production cwd with a mutating argv. Production cwd: an argument whose token stream contains REPO_ROOT, resolved transitively through in-file const/let initializers, so a cwd reached through a variable is caught like a literal. Mutating argv: --retire, --stamp-paid-by, or --split among the argument's string elements, likewise resolved, so a flag arriving through an array, a variable, or a reformat is caught; a plain identifier element that resolves in-file to a flag-free string (the RECORD_REL pattern of the argv-fixture test) is provable and allowed. Refusal, not filtering: an argument shape the scan cannot resolve to provable strings — a spread, a call, a parameter, an import — fails the guard rather than passing it; the guard refuses what it cannot prove, it does not filter it. The bare non-mutating runValidator(REPO_ROOT) calls stay legal. The guard's own predicate is demonstrated in the failing direction on scratch copies before it is trusted: the shipped file as it stands today fails with exactly the two production sites; the same file with the sites removed passes; a mutating argv reaching the call through a variable fails; a reformatted literal with changed spacing fails; a cwd reached through a variable fails; a fixture-cwd call with a mutating variable argv passes; an unresolvable spread element is refused. Scratch under a temporary directory, never the repository tree. The TargetAssertions MustNotContain needles stay as belt-and-braces; they are not the guard, and they stop guarding at the close because an archived plan's assertions are evaluated syntactically only.

Discrimination is shown in the failing direction on a throwaway fixture before the reshaped assertion is trusted: split (one element hand-moved without the other), deletion (an element absent from both files), duplication (an element in both files), and index contradiction (a layer that contradicts the holding file) each fail; the predicate passes both pre-payment and post-move shapes. Scratch files go to a temporary directory, never into the repository working tree; the repository record files are never written by a probe.
